title: 😖 Vikram's query scans ten million rows... the index nobody added #sql #database
title_alts: 🐢 Vikram's email lookup reads every row... what an index actually does #sql #indexing
😤 Vikram indexes every column he has... the write cost nobody counts #sql #indexing
description_hook: A query that was instant on a laptop takes eight seconds in production. The table did not change shape, only size.

claims.claim: read ten million rows to find one
claims.basis: round illustrative table size, stated as an example of a large table
round illustrative assumption, stated as such in the narration
illustrative timing for an unindexed scan; real duration depends on hardware
binary search depth over ten million sorted entries is log base two of ten million, about twenty-four steps
round illustrative size for a table small enough to scan

setting: a small team's production web application

characters.name: Vikram
characters.description: late twenties, short black hair, grey hoodie over a faded tee, thin silver ring on his thumb

scenes.narration: Your database will read ten million rows to find one.
scenes.caption: डेटाबेस १ पंक्ति ढूँढने के लिए करोड़ों पंक्तियाँ पढ़ जाता है
scenes.image_brief: A towering wall of printed table rows stretching upward out of sight, millions of thin grey lines of text on paper, one single row glowing yellow in the middle, cold blue server room light.

scenes.narration: That query felt instant on your laptop. Fifty rows lived there.
scenes.caption: लैपटॉप पर वही क्वेरी तुरंत चली। वहाँ सिर्य़ पचास पंक्तियाँ थीं
scenes.image_brief: A laptop open on a wooden kitchen table showing a short query result of fifty rows of test data, a cooling cup of coffee beside it, warm morning light through a window.

scenes.narration: Production holds millions. The same query now takes eight seconds.
scenes.caption: प्रोडक्शन में लाखों पंक्तियाँ हैं। अब वही क्वेरी आठ सेकंड लेती है
scenes.image_brief: A rack of humming server machines in a cold data centre aisle, a small status screen bolted to the rack showing a spinning progress ring and a timer reading eight seconds, blue white light.

scenes.narration: You will know why one index ends that wait.
scenes.caption: आप जान जाथेंगे कि एक इंडेक्स यह इंतज़ार क्यों ख़त्म कर देता है
scenes.image_brief: A library card catalogue cabinet of narrow wooden drawers, one drawer pulled fully open showing tightly packed alphabetical index cards, warm lamp light on the brass drawer labels.

scenes.narration: With no index the engine checks every row in order.
scenes.caption: इंडेक्स न हो तो इंजन हर पंक्ति को क्रम से जाँचता है
scenes.image_brief: A long row of identical cardboard file boxes on a concrete warehouse floor, every lid lifted off and stacked in a line beside them, papers spilling from each open box, bare overhead bulbs.

scenes.narration: An index keeps that column sorted, so lookups jump ahead.
scenes.caption: इंडेक्स उस कॉलम को क्रम में रखता है, तो खोज सीधे आगे कूदती है
scenes.image_brief: A single wooden catalogue drawer filled with alphabetically sorted cards of email addresses, a tall metal tab marker standing up halfway along the run of cards, warm lamp light.

scenes.narration: Ten million users. One email lookup. No index means ten million reads.
scenes.caption: करोड़ों यूज़र, एक ईमेल की खोज, इंडेक्स नहीं — करोड़ों रीड
scenes.image_brief: An enormous continuous printout of email addresses unspooling across a dark office floor and out through a doorway, one address circled in red far down the paper, harsh overhead light.

scenes.narration: Index that email column. The same lookup now touches about twenty-four rows.
scenes.caption: ईमेल कॉलम पर इंडेक्स बनाओ। अब खोज लगभग चौबीस पंक्तियाँ ही पढ़ती है
scenes.image_brief: About two dozen index cards laid out in a neat fan on a dark desk beside a closed wooden catalogue drawer, the vast paper printout rolled up and set aside, focused desk lamp light.

scenes.narration: Indexes are not free. Every insert must update them too.
scenes.caption: इंडेक्स मुफ़्त नहीं हैं। हर इंसर्ट पर उन्हें भी बदलना पड़ता है
scenes.image_brief: Two identical wooden catalogue drawers packed past capacity, new cards wedged in and bowing upward, a small pile of extra cards waiting on top of the cabinet, cool daylight.

scenes.narration: On two hundred rows? Skip it. Scanning is already cheap.
scenes.caption: दो सौ पंक्तियाँ हैं? ज़रूरत नहीं। पूरा स्कैन पहले से ही सस्ता है
scenes.image_brief: A tiny two drawer wooden card box holding a couple of hundred cards standing on a plain table next to a huge empty steel filing cabinet, warm afternoon light across the table.

scenes.narration: The slow query was never bad code. It read too much.
scenes.caption: धीमी क्वेरी की वजह ख़राब कोड नहीं थी। वह बहुत ज़्यादा पढ़ रही थी
scenes.image_brief: A stopwatch resting on a printed listing of a short clean SQL query, a thick stack of unread paper shoved to one side of the desk, soft desk light.

scenes.narration: Speed comes from reading less, not from a bigger server.
scenes.caption: रफ़्तार कम पढ़ने से आती है, बड़े सर्वर से नहीं
scenes.image_brief: A small neatly sorted index card box open on a table beside an oversized dusty unplugged server tower lying on its side, even flat daylight.

scenes.narration: Run EXPLAIN on your slowest query. Hunt for the full scan.
scenes.caption: अपनी सबसे धीमी क्वेरी पर EXPLAIN चलाओ। फ़ुल स्कैन ढूँढो
scenes.image_brief: A monitor on a dark desk showing a query plan listing with the words FULL TABLE SCAN highlighted in red on one line, the rest of the room unlit, screen glow spilling onto the desk.

title: 😵 Lata's page fires two hundred queries... the join she skipped #sql #backend
title_alts: 🐌 Lata's list page hides an N plus one query... what one join fixes #sql #backend
😬 Lata loops a query for every row... the latency mistake to catch #sql #performance
description_hook: The page looks simple and the queries all look cheap. It is the number of them that costs you.

claims.claim: fired two hundred and one queries
claims.basis: arithmetic of the pattern described: one list query plus one query per row for two hundred rows

claims.claim: Two hundred orders means two hundred extra lookups
claims.basis: round illustrative page size, stated as an example

claims.claim: At two milliseconds each, that is four hundred milliseconds of waiting
claims.basis: arithmetic from the stated figures: two hundred lookups times two milliseconds
illustrative count of tables, used to describe fan out rather than measure it

claims.claim: Anything above ten needs a look
claims.basis: round illustrative threshold offered as a rule of thumb, not a measured limit

setting: an order dashboard in a growing online shop

characters.name: Lata
characters.description: early thirties, long hair tied back, olive green shirt with rolled sleeves, reading glasses pushed up on her head

scenes.narration: One page load fired two hundred and one queries.
scenes.caption: एक पेज लोड ने दो सौ एक क्वेरियाँ चला दीं
scenes.image_brief: A network log printed on a long till roll of paper curling off a desk, hundreds of nearly identical query lines listed one after another, cool white overhead light.

scenes.narration: You fetch a list of orders. That is one query.
scenes.caption: आप ऑर्डर की सूची लाते हैं। यह एक क्वेरी हुई
scenes.image_brief: A single sheet of paper on a clean desk listing twenty order numbers in a tidy column, a pencil laid across the top edge, soft daylight from the left.

scenes.narration: Then your code loops and asks for each customer name.
scenes.caption: फिर कोड लूप करके हर ग्राहक का नाम अलग से पूंछता है
scenes.image_brief: A wall of small paper request slips pinned in a long line across a corkboard, each slip carrying one customer number, a single empty pin waiting at the end, flat office light.

scenes.narration: You will spot this pattern and collapse it into one.
scenes.caption: आप यह पैटर्न पहचानेंगे और उसे एक क्वेरी में समेट देंगे
scenes.image_brief: Two hundred paper slips gathered into one thick stapled bundle sitting on a desk beside the empty corkboard they came from, warm lamp light on the bundle.

scenes.narration: Every round trip to the database costs waiting time, not work.
scenes.caption: डेटाबेस तक हर चक्कर काम नहीं, इंतज़ार ख़र्च करता है
scenes.image_brief: A pneumatic tube running between two rooms with a single capsule travelling through it, one empty counter at each end, everything else in the rooms still, cool even light.

scenes.narration: A join asks once and lets the database do the matching.
scenes.caption: जॉइन एक बार पूंछता है और मिलान का काम डेटाबेस पर छोड़ता है
scenes.image_brief: Two printed tables laid side by side on a large table, coloured threads stretched between matching order numbers and customer numbers, threads pinned taut, bright even light.

scenes.narration: Two hundred orders means two hundred extra lookups. Add the first.
scenes.caption: दो सौ ऑर्डर यानी दो सौ अतिरिक्त लुकअप। पहली क्वेरी अलग
scenes.image_brief: Two hundred small paper slips spread in a dense grid across a wooden floor with one larger sheet placed apart from them at the top, plain overhead light.

scenes.narration: At two milliseconds each, that is four hundred milliseconds of waiting.
scenes.caption: हर एक दो मिलीसेकंड, यानी कुल चार सौ मिलीसेकंड का इंतज़ार
scenes.image_brief: A large mechanical stopwatch on a desk with its hand stopped just past the four hundred millisecond mark, a loading spinner frozen on a screen behind it, dim room light.

scenes.narration: One join is not always right. Joining six tables duplicates rows.
scenes.caption: हर बार जॉइन सही नहीं। छह टेबल जोड़ने से पंक्तियाँ दोहरा जाती हैं
scenes.image_brief: Six printed tables overlapping in a messy heap with tangled coloured threads running between all of them, duplicate rows fanning out at the edge of the pile, harsh light.

scenes.narration: So the slow page was never the query. It was the count.
scenes.caption: तो धीमे पेज की वजह क्वेरी नहीं थी। उनकी गिनती थी
scenes.image_brief: One short tidy query printed on a single card propped upright in front of a toppled mountain of identical request slips, warm focused light on the card.

scenes.narration: Ask once for everything you need. Latency stops multiplying.
scenes.caption: जो चाहिए वह एक ही बार माँगो। तब देरी गुना नहीं होती
scenes.image_brief: A single capsule arriving in a pneumatic tube station carrying one thick folded document, the receiving counter otherwise empty and clean, calm morning light.

scenes.narration: Log your query count per page. Anything above ten needs a look.
scenes.caption: हर पेज की क्वेरी गिनती लॉग करो। दस से ऊपर हो तो देखो
scenes.image_brief: A small dashboard panel on a monitor showing a single counter labelled queries per request with the number twelve on it, dim office at night, screen glow on the keyboard.

title: 😱 Imran's UPDATE skipped its WHERE line... the two words that undo it #sql #transactions
title_alts: 🧯 Imran wraps every UPDATE in a transaction... what commit really means #sql #transactions
😬 Imran forgot one WHERE clause... the SELECT check that saves the table #sql #sqltips
description_hook: An UPDATE with no filter matches every row in the table. There is a habit that makes that survivable.

claims.claim: the two words that undo it
claims.basis: counts the words named later in the script, BEGIN and ROLLBACK
round illustrative catalogue size, stated as an example
describes a step rather than a measured figure

setting: the product catalogue of a warehouse retailer

characters.name: Imran
characters.description: mid thirties, close cropped beard, navy zip jacket over a white shirt, lanyard with a scratched access card

scenes.narration: A missing WHERE clause repriced the entire catalogue.
scenes.caption: ग़ायब WHERE लाइन ने पूरी कैटलॉग की कीमतें बदल दीं
scenes.image_brief: A long warehouse shelf lined with hundreds of retail price tags, every single tag printed with the same identical number, cold fluorescent light down the aisle.

scenes.narration: You meant to change one product. The WHERE line never ran.
scenes.caption: आप एक ही प्रोडक्ट बदलना चाहते थे। WHERE लाइन चली ही नहीं
scenes.image_brief: A printed SQL statement on a sheet of paper showing an UPDATE line and a SET line, with an empty gap where the WHERE line should be, a red pen resting beside it, dim desk light.

scenes.narration: You will learn the two words that make this reversible.
scenes.caption: आप वे दो शब्द सीखेंगे जिनसे यह ग़लती वापस पलटी जा सकती है
scenes.image_brief: A glass jar standing on a desk holding a single folded paper slip with the word ROLLBACK written on it, warm lamp light glowing behind the jar.

scenes.narration: UPDATE touches every row that matches. With no filter, everything matches.
scenes.caption: UPDATE हर मिलती पंक्ति बदलता है। फ़िल्टर न हो तो सब मिलती हैं
scenes.image_brief: Thousands of product cards spread edge to edge across a warehouse floor, each one stamped with the same price in fresh red ink, not one card left unstamped, bright overhead light.

scenes.narration: Wrap it in a transaction. Nothing is final until you commit.
scenes.caption: इसे ट्रांज़ैक्शन में लपेटो। कमिट तक कुछ भी पक्का नहीं होता
scenes.image_brief: A workbench holding a soft wet clay tablet with fresh writing pressed into it, a cold empty kiln standing open beside the bench, warm side light on the damp clay.

scenes.narration: Forty thousand products. One statement. Every price becomes the same.
scenes.caption: चालीस हज़ार प्रोडक्ट। एक स्टेटमेंट। हर कीमत एक जैसी हो गई
scenes.image_brief: One short printed statement pinned to the end of a tall warehouse shelving unit, and every price tag on the shelves below it showing one identical number, harsh aisle light.

scenes.narration: Inside a transaction you check the row count first, then roll back.
scenes.caption: ट्रांज़ैक्शन के अंदर पहले पंक्तियों की गिनती देखो, फिर रोलबैक करो
scenes.image_brief: A monitor in a dark room showing a message that reads forty thousand rows affected, with the word ROLLBACK typed on the line beneath it, screen glow on the desk.

scenes.narration: Transactions do not save you after a commit. Then only backups do.
scenes.caption: कमिट के बाद ट्रांज़ैक्शन नहीं बचाता। तब सिर्य़ बैकअप काम आता है
scenes.image_brief: A heavy steel deposit box bolted shut on a concrete floor with COMMITTED stencilled on its lid, a single tape backup cartridge on a shelf above it, one dim bulb overhead.

scenes.narration: The danger was never the UPDATE. It was running it alone.
scenes.caption: ख़तरा UPDATE नहीं था। उसे अकेले चलाना ख़तरा था
scenes.image_brief: A single product price tag standing upright in a small clamp on an otherwise bare workbench, a heap of identical discarded tags pushed to the far corner, soft light.

scenes.narration: Write the SELECT first. Same WHERE line, same rows, no damage.
scenes.caption: पहले SELECT लिखो। वही WHERE, वही पंक्तियाँ, कोई नुक़सान नहीं
scenes.image_brief: Two printed statements lying side by side on a clean desk, the first starting with SELECT and the second with UPDATE, the identical WHERE line on each marked in green, daylight.

scenes.narration: Before your next UPDATE, run it as a SELECT and count.
scenes.caption: अगले UPDATE से पहले उसे SELECT बनाकर चलाओ और गिनो
scenes.image_brief: A monitor showing a SELECT query with a result count of one row underneath it, a yellow sticky note on the screen bezel reading COUNT FIRST, dim evening room.

title: 🤨 Suhana's NULL filter returns zero rows... the operator she needed #sql #nulls
title_alts: 🔍 Suhana counts a column full of blanks... what COUNT quietly ignores #sql #nulls
😒 Suhana counts blanks as NULL... the audit that catches both kinds #sql #dataquality
description_hook: The blank rows are right there in the table, and the filter still returns nothing. NULL is not a value you can compare.

claims.basis: round illustrative table size, stated as an example

claims.claim: Three hundred have no phone number stored
claims.basis: round illustrative share of blank rows, stated as an example

claims.claim: COUNT of phone returns seven hundred
claims.basis: arithmetic from the stated figures: one thousand rows minus three hundred blanks

setting: a customer records table in a clinic booking system

characters.name: Suhana
characters.description: early twenties, dark curls cut short, mustard cardigan over a plain kurta, pencil tucked behind one ear

scenes.narration: In SQL, nothing equals nothing. Not even itself.
scenes.caption: SQL में कुछ भी किसी के बराबर नहीं। ख़ुद के भी नहीं
scenes.image_brief: Two completely blank paper forms facing each other on a dark table with an equals sign built from two short metal rods lying between them, cold overhead light.

scenes.narration: You filter for rows where the phone column equals NULL.
scenes.caption: आप वे पंक्तियाँ छानते हैं जहाँ फ़ोन कॉलम NULL के बराबर हो
scenes.image_brief: A paper customer record card with the phone field left completely blank, a magnifying glass resting directly on that empty field, warm desk lamp light.

scenes.narration: The query returns zero rows. The empty rows are still there.
scenes.caption: क्वेरी शून्य पंक्तियाँ देती है। ख़ाली पंक्तियाँ वहीं मौजूद हैं
scenes.image_brief: A screen showing a results panel that reads zero rows returned, and on the desk in front of it a tray of customer cards with visibly blank phone lines, dim room.

scenes.narration: You will know why, and the operator that actually works.
scenes.caption: आप वजह जानेंगे और वह ऑपरेटर भी जो असल में काम करता है
scenes.image_brief: A wooden rubber stamp lying on a desk with the words IS NULL carved into its face, fresh dark ink on the rubber, a stack of customer cards beside it, warm lamp light.

scenes.narration: NULL means unknown, not empty. Unknown cannot equal unknown.
scenes.caption: NULL का मतलब अज्ञात है, ख़ाली नहीं। अज्ञात अज्ञात के बराबर नहीं
scenes.image_brief: Two identical sealed cardboard boxes standing side by side on a grey floor, a large question mark painted on each one, both boxes taped shut, plain flat light.

scenes.narration: So the comparison returns unknown, and unknown rows get filtered out.
scenes.caption: तो तुलना अज्ञात देती है, और वे पंक्तियाँ बाहर छँट जाती हैं
scenes.image_brief: A metal sorting chute dropping cards into three labelled bins marked TRUE, FALSE and UNKNOWN, the unknown bin overflowing onto the floor while the other two sit nearly empty, cool light.

scenes.narration: One thousand customers. Three hundred have no phone number stored.
scenes.caption: एक हज़ार ग्राहक। तीन सौ का फ़ोन नंबर दर्ज ही नहीं है
scenes.image_brief: One thousand customer cards stacked in ten neat blocks along a long table, three of those blocks pulled forward with their blank phone lines showing, even daylight.

scenes.narration: COUNT of phone returns seven hundred. IS NULL finds the rest.
scenes.caption: COUNT फ़ोन सात सौ देता है। बाक़ी IS NULL से मिलते हैं
scenes.image_brief: Two mechanical tally counters on a wooden desk, the larger one reading seven hundred and the smaller one reading three hundred, warm side light across the desk.

scenes.narration: An empty string is not NULL. It is a real value.
scenes.caption: ख़ाली स्ट्रिंग NULL नहीं है। वह एक असली मान है
scenes.image_brief: Two envelopes lying on a table, one flattened and sealed with nothing inside it, and next to it only a clean dust outline where an envelope used to be, soft window light.

scenes.narration: So both can hide in one column. Check for each separately.
scenes.caption: दोनों एक ही कॉलम में छिप सकते हैं। हर एक को अलग जाँचो
scenes.image_brief: A single column of customer cards standing in a rack where some cards are entirely blank paper and others carry a printed pair of quote marks with nothing between them, cool light.

scenes.narration: NULL is not a value. It is the absence of one.
scenes.caption: NULL कोई मान नहीं है। वह मान के न होने का निशान है
scenes.image_brief: A bare picture hook on a plain painted wall with a clean unfaded rectangle around it where a frame hung for years, soft afternoon light across the wall.

scenes.narration: Count what exists. Then count what is missing. Different questions.
scenes.caption: जो मौजूद है उसे गिनो। फिर जो ग़ायब है। सवाल अलग हैं
scenes.image_brief: Two clipboards propped on a desk, one headed WHAT WE HAVE holding a thick stack of filled forms, the other headed WHAT IS MISSING holding blank sheets, even daylight.

scenes.narration: Audit one column tonight. Compare COUNT star with COUNT that column.
scenes.caption: आज एक कॉलम जाँचो। COUNT स्टार और COUNT कॉलम की तुलना करो
scenes.image_brief: A monitor in a dark room showing two result numbers side by side, one labelled COUNT star and one labelled COUNT phone, the two numbers clearly different, screen glow on the keys.

title: 📈 Deepak's revenue report doubled... the JOIN that repeats every row #sql #joins
title_alts: 🧵 Deepak joins orders to items in a report... what fan out does to SUM #sql #joins
😓 Deepak sums an order total after a join... the double count to avoid #sql #reporting
description_hook: Every number in the table is correct and the report still reads twice the truth. A join changed how many times each row appears.

claims.basis: illustrative outcome for the three item example that follows, not a measured figure

claims.claim: One order totalling fifty holds three items
claims.basis: round illustrative order used as the worked example
arithmetic from the stated figures: a total of fifty repeated across three joined rows

setting: a weekly sales report at a small online shop

characters.name: Deepak
characters.description: forties, receding hairline, checked shirt with a pen in the pocket, thick black rimmed glasses

scenes.narration: Your revenue report is double. The data is fine.
scenes.caption: आपकी रेवेन्यू रिपोर्ट दोगुनी है। डेटा में कोई ग़लती नहीं
scenes.image_brief: Two printed revenue reports lying side by side on a desk, the grand total on the right one exactly twice the total on the left, a red pen across both pages, plain desk light.

scenes.narration: You joined orders to order items to get product names.
scenes.caption: आपने प्रोडक्ट नाम पाने के लिए ऑर्डर को ऑर्डर आइटम से जोड़ा
scenes.image_brief: Two printed tables laid flat on a large wooden table, one headed ORDERS and one headed ORDER ITEMS, a red string tying a single order number across to three item rows, bright light.

scenes.narration: Then you summed the order total. It came back inflated.
scenes.caption: फिर आपने ऑर्डर टोटल जोड़ा। जवाब बढ़ा हुआ आया
scenes.image_brief: A long paper tape curling out of a mechanical adding machine onto a desk, the printed total at the end of the tape circled in red, warm office light.

scenes.narration: You will see where the extra money came from.
scenes.caption: आप देखेंगे कि वह अतिरिक्त रक़म कहाँ से आई
scenes.image_brief: One paper receipt slip sitting on the glass bed of an open photocopier with three identical copies of it laid out in a row beside the machine, cool light from the copier lamp.

scenes.narration: A join repeats the left row once per match on the right.
scenes.caption: जॉइन बाईं पंक्ति को दाईं तरफ़ के हर मिलान पर दोहराता है
scenes.image_brief: One printed order row copied three times and fanned out in a stack on a table, each copy paired with a different item card beside it, even overhead light.

scenes.narration: Summing a repeated column adds the same money several times.
scenes.caption: दोहराए कॉलम को जोड़ने से वही रक़म कई बार जुड़ जाती है
scenes.image_brief: Three identical paper slips each showing the same total piled onto one pan of a brass balance scale, that pan sunk low while the other rises, warm side light.

scenes.narration: One order totalling fifty holds three items. The join makes three rows.
scenes.caption: पचास का एक ऑर्डर, तीन आइटम। जॉइन तीन पंक्तियाँ बनाता है
scenes.image_brief: One paper order card showing a total of fifty laid beside three item cards for socks, a mug and a notebook, all four cards squared up on a wooden table, daylight.

scenes.narration: Sum the order total now and you get one hundred fifty.
scenes.caption: अब ऑर्डर टोटल जोड़ो तो कुल एक सौ पचास आता है
scenes.image_brief: A mechanical calculator on a desk with one hundred fifty showing in its display, three identical order slips fanned out in front of it, warm lamp light.

scenes.narration: Nothing here is a bug. The join did exactly what you asked.
scenes.caption: यह कोई बग नहीं है। जॉइन ने वही किया जो आपने माँगा
scenes.image_brief: A printed query listing on a clean desk with a green tick stamped next to the JOIN line and no error marks anywhere on the page, calm even light.

scenes.narration: Sum at the level the number lives. Totals belong to orders.
scenes.caption: जोड़ उसी स्तर पर करो जहाँ वह संख्या रहती है। टोटल ऑर्डर का है
scenes.image_brief: Two labelled trays on a desk, one marked ONE ROW PER ORDER holding neat single cards and one marked ONE ROW PER ITEM holding thick bundles of cards, daylight.

scenes.narration: Items get their own sum. One grain per query.
scenes.caption: आइटम का जोड़ अलग होता है। एक क्वेरी, एक स्तर
scenes.image_brief: A single measuring jug labelled orders standing beside a row of small identical cups labelled items on a kitchen counter, soft window light.

scenes.narration: Check one report today. Does its row count match the orders?
scenes.caption: आज एक रिपोर्ट देखो। उसकी पंक्तियाँ ऑर्डर से मेल खाती हैं?
scenes.image_brief: A monitor showing two counts stacked in a results panel, one labelled rows in report and one labelled orders, the two numbers clearly different, dim room, screen glow.

title: 🐌 Rekha's page five hundred crawls... the OFFSET cost nobody measures #sql #pagination
title_alts: 🔎 Rekha pages a long list with LIMIT OFFSET... what seek paging fixes #sql #pagination
😕 Rekha lets users jump to any deep page... the paging habit to drop #sql #performance
description_hook: The first page of a list opens instantly and a deep page takes seconds. OFFSET is doing work you never see.

claims.basis: round illustrative page size, stated as an example

claims.claim: Page five hundred means offset ten thousand
claims.basis: arithmetic from the stated figures: five hundred pages of twenty rows

claims.claim: That is ten thousand rows discarded
claims.basis: follows from the offset already stated, since OFFSET reads then discards those rows
follows from the stated page size of twenty when the query seeks by the last id

setting: an archive browser with a very long result list

characters.name: Rekha
characters.description: late twenties, straight shoulder length hair, rust coloured kurta with sleeves pushed up, plain steel wristwatch

scenes.narration: Page one loads fast. Page five hundred crawls.
scenes.caption: पहला पेज तेज़ खुलता है। पाँच सौवाँ पेज घिसटता है
scenes.image_brief: Two stopwatches on a dark desk, the left one stopped near the start of its dial and the right one stopped far around it, small cards beside them reading page one and page five hundred, plain light.

scenes.narration: Your list uses LIMIT twenty and OFFSET whatever page they clicked.
scenes.caption: आपकी सूची LIMIT बीस और पेज नंबर वाले OFFSET से चलती है
scenes.image_brief: A printed query on a sheet of paper reading LIMIT twenty OFFSET, with a page number written beside it in pencil and a list of page links printed below, soft desk light.

scenes.narration: You will learn why deep pages get slower, and the fix.
scenes.caption: आप जानेंगे कि गहरे पेज धीमे क्यों होते हैं, और इलाज क्या है
scenes.image_brief: A red bookmark ribbon lying across an open ledger page with the last read row underlined in pencil, the rest of the page blank, warm lamp light.

scenes.narration: OFFSET does not skip rows. It reads them, then throws them away.
scenes.caption: OFFSET पंक्तियाँ छोड़ता नहीं। वह उन्हें पढ़कर फेंक देता है
scenes.image_brief: A conveyor belt carrying paper record cards past a counting gate and tipping almost all of them into a large waste bin, only the last few cards continuing to an out tray, cold warehouse light.

scenes.narration: So the deeper the page, the more wasted reading happens.
scenes.caption: पेज जितना गहरा, उतनी ही पढ़ाई बेकार जाती है
scenes.image_brief: Two waste bins standing side by side on a warehouse floor, one holding a thin layer of discarded cards and the other overflowing, labels on their rims reading page ten and page five hundred, dim light.

scenes.narration: Page five hundred means offset ten thousand. That is ten thousand rows discarded.
scenes.caption: पाँच सौवाँ पेज यानी ऑफ़सेट दस हज़ार। दस हज़ार पंक्तियाँ बेकार
scenes.image_brief: An enormous heap of discarded paper rows piled on the floor beside a printer with just twenty fresh rows stacked neatly in the out tray, harsh overhead light.

scenes.narration: Instead ask for rows after the last id you showed. Twenty reads.
scenes.caption: इसके बजाय आख़िरी दिखाई आईडी के बाद की पंक्तियाँ माँगो। बीस रीड
scenes.image_brief: An open ledger with a bookmark ribbon set at one row and exactly twenty rows written in after it, the earlier pages closed flat and untouched, warm lamp light.

scenes.narration: It cannot jump to an arbitrary page. Next and previous only.
scenes.caption: यह किसी भी पेज पर सीधे नहीं कूद सकता। अगला और पिछला ही
scenes.image_brief: A thick ledger with only two paper tabs attached to its edge, one marked NEXT and one marked PREVIOUS, no other tabs along the whole book, even daylight.

scenes.narration: Deep pages were never heavy. The skipping was.
scenes.caption: गहरे पेज भारी नहीं थे। छोड़ने का काम भारी था
scenes.image_brief: A bin of discarded paper rows standing much taller than the small neat stack of kept rows on the desk next to it, plain office light.

scenes.narration: Remember where you stopped. Then read forward from there.
scenes.caption: याद रखो कहाँ रुके थे। फिर वहीं से आगे पढ़ो
scenes.image_brief: A pencil mark under the final written row of a ledger page with a bookmark ribbon laid exactly on that line and the next blank line waiting below, soft light.

scenes.narration: Time page one against page one hundred. Compare the two numbers.
scenes.caption: पेज एक और पेज सौ का समय नापो। दोनों संख्याएँ मिलाओ
scenes.image_brief: A monitor in a dark room showing two timing lines in a terminal, one labelled page one and one labelled page one hundred with a far larger duration, screen glow on the desk.
